title: Jeanne Jugan (30 August)
hookLine: a poor Frenchwoman who took an old blind woman into her own bed and founded the Little Sisters of the Poor
tomorrow: The Holy Name of Mary (12 September)

lines: A STAIRCASE, A ROOM, ONE BED.
A BLIND OLD WOMAN, NOWHERE TO GO.
cards: A narrow staircase. A small room. One bed.

Jeanne Jugan is a poor woman in a seaside town in Brittany, in France, earning her keep with her hands. One winter, the story goes, she comes home carrying an old woman who is blind, widowed, and has nowhere to go.
Jeanne carries her up the stairs, lays her in her own bed, and takes the attic for herself. That's how it begins. Not with a plan, or a building, or money.
With one bed, given away. Today, the woman behind the Little Sisters of the Poor.

teach.b: One old woman became two, then more. A few younger women joined Jeanne, and they called themselves sisters. But they had nothing to feed anyone with.
So Jeanne picked up a basket and went begging, door to door, for her old people: food, coins, scraps, whatever people would give. Tradition remembers her knocking, being refused, and coming back.
It wasn't humiliating to her, the story goes; it was the work.

teach.h: THE LITTLE SISTERS OF THE POOR.
teach.b: The community grew into the Little Sisters of the Poor, homes where the poor and the old could live and die with someone beside them.
Jesus says, in the Douay-Rheims: "as long as you did it to one of these my least brethren, you did it to me." Jeanne lived that line one bed at a time. Then the hidden half of her story.

teach.h: SET ASIDE BY HER OWN COMMUNITY.
teach.b: A priest who helped direct the young community took control of it. Jeanne, the founder, was removed as its head and sent to live quietly in the motherhouse, doing small tasks among the novices.
For a long time, the young sisters arriving weren't told that she had begun it all. She didn't fight it.
Tradition remembers her telling the novices to be little, and to stay little.
Only later was she recognized as the founder, and later still the Church named her a saint.
So her life gives the word old two meanings: the old people she served, and her own old age, spent hidden, with nothing to show for what she'd built. Catholics see both as given to God.

how: Catholics keep the memory of Saint Jeanne Jugan on 30 August; the Little Sisters of the Poor, the congregation she began, run homes for poor elderly people and go out asking for alms to support them.

a nun who nursed soldiers in a French war

s: Jeanne Jugan began with a building and money behind her
she began with one bed, her own, given to a blind old woman.
she led her community for the rest of her life
she was removed as its head and lived quietly, and young sisters weren't told she had founded it.

games.q: you began this community. now a priest has taken it over, set you aside, and the new sisters don't even know it was you. what do you do?
o: tell everyone the truth and demand your place back.
accept it, and live quietly among the novices.
games.why: she stayed, quiet and hidden, telling the novices to be little. only later was she recognized as the founder.

practice: Bring to mind one person whose hair is gray, a grandparent, a neighbor, someone in a care home you drive past, and think about their days: who talks to them, who listens?
If you pray, ask Saint Jeanne Jugan to pray for them; if you don't, simply hold them in mind with care.
